items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee only responds 'Right.' to the interviewer's story about Ben Webster and Jimmy Blanton ('Bear'). There is no evidence in the transcript that Walter P. Thomas personally knew, met, or had a relationship with Jimmy Blanton.

ctx.x: But during this time (I'm listing this because it should be a part of your record), Ben Webster came to me, and said, "Bear..." That's what they called Jimmy Blanton. He said, "Bear is very sick, and we had to put him in a rest home." He had tuberculosis. He was a beautiful young man of 22 years old who didn't drink or smoke, but he was very frail, and being in Duke Ellington's band and making those one-night stands and getting soaking wet, playing as hard as he played and as fabulous as he played, and taking…

And Ben suggested that I...since we were coming out on the same engagement, and Duke's band was leaving, they were leaving town... He said, "Be sure and look out for Bear" -- Blanton. And in those days, remember, we had no penicillin; this is before penicillin. I don't even think the sulfur drugs were even too prevalent. But anyway, the only thing they were doing for tuberculosis in those days was just rest, bed rest -- which was not quite enough for what he had contracted.
